prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single, objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car wreck — the right lawyer depends on the specifics of your crash, injuries, insurance issues and what outcome you want (quick fair settlement vs. taking to trial). I can help you find strong candidates, but first here are practical ways to pick the best lawyer for your case and some next steps.

What to look for
- Substantial car-accident experience: look for many years and a track record handling similar wrecks (rear-end, T-bone, multi-car, catastrophic injury, uninsured/underinsured motorist).
- Trial experience: many cases settle, but you want a lawyer who will actually try the case if the insurer won’t pay fair value.
- Resources: firms that can hire accident reconstructionists, medical experts and handle medical liens.
- Client results & reputation: past settlements/verdicts, peer recognition (Super Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell), client reviews.
- Board certification: Texas Board of Legal Specialization offers certification in Personal Injury Trial Law — that’s a meaningful credential.
- Communication and team: who will handle your file, how often you’ll get updates, and how accessible they are.
- Fee structure: most PI lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you win). Ask percentage, who pays costs up front, and how costs are repaid.

Where to search and check background
- Texas State Bar “Find a Lawyer” (disciplinary history)
- Super Lawyers and Martindale-Hubbell (peer ratings)
- Avvo, Google and Yelp for client reviews
- Local Houston Bar Association referrals

Questions to ask in a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the results?
- How many car-accident cases have you tried?
- Who will handle my case day‑to‑day?
- What is your fee and how are costs handled?
- What is a realistic range for my case and timeline?
- Will you advance medical lien payments and other costs?
- Do you get paid only if I recover?

Typical fee expectations
- Contingency fees commonly 33%–40% (may be higher if the case goes to trial). Confirm in writing.

Quick next steps
1. If you haven’t already, get a copy of the police report and keep all medical records/receipts.
2. Contact 3–5 attorneys for free consultations and compare answers to the questions above.
3. Ask each for references and recent similar case results.

If you’d like, tell me:
- ZIP code or neighborhood in Houston
- Date of the crash, severity of injuries, whether fault/insurance is disputed
I can then pull a short list (3–5) of highly rated Houston personal injury lawyers/firms for you to contact.
